question: Does diagonal passive evidence plus a two-intervention budget suffice to identify previously unknown 3-input Boolean causal laws? Which probes have positive decision value after cost?
hypothesis: With passive actions limited to 000 and 111 and their outputs fixed 0 and 1, 64 distinct Boolean causal laws remain observationally equivalent. Any two noiseless distinct additional binary probes leave at least 16 such laws consistent. For a uniform unstructured prior, a probe outside the terminal decision pair cannot improve terminal expected utility; net value is negative after strictly positive probe costs.

predecessor_evidence.note: YNCA04 exact dual-OS development negative with cost-aware probes; model used 12 passive events largely on diagonal and at most two probes; no source/seed reuse

inputs.name: All 256 three-input binary truth tables; restrict f(000)=0,f(111)=1; analyze exact 64 candidate tables

frozen_design.conditioning: f(000)=0, f(111)=1 -> 64 distinct laws; six unconstrained off-diagonal truth bits
frozen_design.terminal_options: all 15 unordered distinct pairs among actions 1..6, equal weight
frozen_design.terminal_utility: true binary outcome at selected terminal action minus 0.08 per active input bit
frozen_design.probe_cost: 0.018+0.012*number of active input bits; strictly positive for every action
first_action_policy_set: oracle expected terminal value minus probe cost
choose the cheapest candidate terminal action
primary_metrics: exact number of passively indistinguishable laws
minimum residual indistinguishable laws after any two noiseless probes
count of terminal decision pairs with positive net value of probing
exact average regret-plus-probe-cost over all 15 pairs for each policy
frozen_design.scoring: Enumerate all 64 laws, all 15 candidate terminal pairs, all four ordered two-outcome sequences, and exact Bayesian likelihood/posterior updates (rational probabilities), with zero external/train/heldout data. Use deterministic arithmetic and fixed sorted tie break.
frozen_design.comparison: Analytic exact Bayes decision-value oracle is a theoretical comparator, not a trainable learner. Stop, random, cheapest candidate, and fixed action controls share same 2-sample budget and actual cost accounting.
frozen_design.resource_budget: Python 3.12 standard library, 10 seconds typical for complete exact analysis, GitHub Actions hosted Linux and Windows only, no paid APIs.
frozen_design.classification_rules: The mathematical bound is PROVEN_ANALYTIC only if 64 laws/16 residual after 2 probes and zero information gain for off-pair probes are validated exhaustively. A cost-aware decision policy is better than controls only if exact mean net utility dominates every fixed and randomized action; no native-model scientific pass is possible from this analytic task.
frozen_design.source_first_use: Pin experiment.py SHA256 and source commit before primary analytic result/CI; no parameter tuning after output.

controls: Exact Bayesian myopic value of decision information
metrics: Residual class sizes for all probe subsets
Number of pairs with positive net probe utility
Full mean terminal risk plus probe cost by policy
Correctness checks against brute-force law enumeration
Full OS and exact SHA receipts

classification_rules.supported: ANALYTIC_PROOF_SUPPORTED if exhaustive independent checks establish observational equivalence cardinality and strict negative value for off-terminal-pair probes, with both OS reproducibility. Does not imply scientific intelligence gain.
classification_rules.mixed: Disagreement between independent combinatorial and Bayesian enumerators, or incomplete exact controls: UNVERIFIED, no promotion.
classification_rules.negative: If any of the two named identifiability bounds is disproven, ANALYTIC_HYPOTHESIS_FALSE; retain result without changing hypothesis.
classification_rules.invalid: Any source/result identity mismatch, omitted laws/controls, or post-output source changes invalidates confirmatory status.

preregistration_note: Exact exhaustive analytic source locked before primary output. No models trained and no original source-science first-use; algorithmic equivalence proof only.
